firstLaunch.title: Before you start
body: After is a story you read and play, one screen at a time, with small things to try in real life.
It's a companion for a hard time. It isn't therapy, and it doesn't replace a doctor, a therapist or the people who love you.
Everything you write stays on this phone. Nobody else can read it.
If things ever feel like too much, tap "I'm not okay" in the top corner of any screen.
firstLaunch.personTitle: One person you could message on a bad day
firstLaunch.personHint: Optional. You can change it later.

notOkay.title: You don't have to be okay.
notOkay.intro: Here are three things you can do right now. Any one of them is enough.
notOkay.messageBody: Hey, I'm having a really hard time. Can you call me?
notOkay.noPerson: Save one person you could message

why.title: Why this exists
body: I made this for my brother, after his first heartbreak.
I couldn't be there every night, and I didn't always know what to say. So I made something that could be: a story about someone going through the same thing, and the small things that actually help.
If someone gave you this link, it's because they care about you, too.

name.title: Who is the hero?
name.body: The story follows a young man in a new city, the week after his girlfriend leaves. In the story he's called {default}, but you can give him your own name, or any name you like.
name.hint: You can change it later from the menu.

items.title: Story
items.text: Tap to read, one line at a time. Swipe right to go back. Sometimes you choose what happens, or try something small for real. Each chapter ends with a quest in real life, and the next chapter opens when you've done it.

items.title: What to do when
items.text: Help for hard moments: when you want to text her, can't sleep, can't eat, feel alone. With videos that may help.

items.title: Habits
items.text: Small things that keep you steady. Start the ones you want, track them if you like, or add your own.

items.title: I'm not okay
items.text: Top right, on every screen. A helpline, a message to someone you trust, and a breathing exercise.

items.title: Sound
items.text: Music and read-aloud, both off unless you turn them on.

facts.title: Why this matters

items.text: More than 720,000 people die by suicide every year around the world.
It's the third leading cause of death for people aged 15 to 29.
In France, 9,300 people died by suicide in 2016. Three out of four were men.

after: Men are less likely to ask for help, and experts see that as one of the reasons so many more men die by suicide. It's also why this app keeps nudging you towards people.
Suicide can be prevented. Talking helps, and help is there, any time:

ladder: Say one true thing about yourself

places._note: DRAFT, please edit: suggestions shown at 3.30, by energy (low/some/high) and talk (near/little/talk).

low-near.name: A library reading room
low-near.why: People around you, no one expects you to talk.

low-near.name: The same café, same table
low-near.why: Being seen counts. Bring a book.

low-near.name: A park bench at the same hour
low-near.why: The regulars will start to recognise you.

low-little.name: A café counter
low-little.why: Small talk with the barista, and you can leave any time.

low-little.name: A museum's free evening
low-little.why: Something to look at together, and to talk about if you want.

low-talk.name: A support or grief group
low-talk.why: Everyone there knows why you came.

low-talk.name: A small evening class
low-talk.why: Same people every week, with a task to share.

some-near.name: A yoga or stretching class
some-near.why: Side by side, no talking needed.

some-near.name: A swimming pool
some-near.why: Same lane, same time, same faces.

some-near.name: A Saturday market
some-near.why: Busy and friendly, at your own pace.

some-little.name: A volunteering shift
some-little.why: Working side by side makes talking easy.

some-little.name: A climbing or bouldering gym
some-little.why: People chat between climbs, and help each other.

some-little.name: A cooking or pottery class
some-little.why: Hands busy, words come by themselves.

some-talk.name: A language exchange
some-talk.why: Everyone is there to talk, and everyone is a bit awkward.

some-talk.name: A book club
some-talk.why: The book gives you something to say.

high-near.name: A running club
high-near.why: Run together, coffee after if you like.

high-near.name: A choir
high-near.why: Singing with others, no small talk required.

high-talk.name: A community kitchen or supper club
Start something yourself
high-talk.why: A walk, a game night, a soup. Ask one person to come.
